key_insight: The paper introduces quantum probabilistic local differential privacy (QPLDP), a relaxed privacy notion that allows rare spectral privacy violations while preserving useful structural and sample-complexity guarantees.
engineering_relevance: QPLDP gives quantum ML and quantum information systems a more flexible privacy framework for noisy quantum channels, with direct implications for private hypothesis testing and privacy-preserving quantum protocols.
method: Defines QPLDP as a probabilistic relaxation of quantum local differential privacy via quantum privacy-loss violation events.
Proves structural properties under tensor-product composition and unitary post-processing, and shows it is generally not convex or closed under arbitrary quantum-channel post-processing.
Derives lower bounds via hockey-stick divergence and applies them to sample complexity in asymmetric and symmetric quantum hypothesis testing.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical analysis and derived bounds across representative scenarios, including characterizations for depolarizing noise and sample-complexity results for quantum hypothesis testing.
watch_item: Because QPLDP can fail under arbitrary post-processing and is not convex, practical deployments must carefully control channel composition and downstream transformations.
paper_title: Quantum Probabilistic Local Differential Privacy: Structural Properties and Sample Complexity Bounds
